question.problem:
Consider the following geometric sequence:

$$
{a}_{n+1}=\frac{1}{4}{a}_{n},\,{a}_{1}=256,\,n\ge 1
$$

The $4$th term of this geometric sequence is ${a}_{4}=$
{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
We use the recursive formula to compute the terms of the sequence up to the $4$th term:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} & =256 \\ {a}_{2} & =\frac{1}{4}{a}_{1}=\frac{1}{4}(256)=64 \\ {a}_{3} & =\frac{1}{4}{a}_{2}=\frac{1}{4}(64)=16 \\ {a}_{4} & =\frac{1}{4}{a}_{3}=\frac{1}{4}(16)=4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${a}_{4}=4.$
